title: Washington AI Laws

reading.body:
Washington has enacted one AI-related law, HB2225, regulating companion chatbots through disclosure, minor protections, and self-harm response protocols.

The law is narrow in scope. It does not govern AI in hiring, lending, housing, medical diagnosis, or government decision-making. It targets a single consumer product category, the companion chatbot, and regulates it through transparency and safety requirements rather than through restrictions on model capability or deployment. The obligations fall on operators: disclose that the chatbot is artificial, notify users repeatedly, restrict sexually explicit content and manipulative engagement for minors, and maintain and publish protocols for suicidal ideation and self-harm.

For AI infrastructure, the relevance is indirect. A law like this does not constrain data center siting, power procurement, or compute supply. It constrains what a deployed model must say and do at the interface. That matters because compliance obligations of this kind are served by inference-time systems, content classifiers, and human review pipelines, all of which run on the same compute the rest of the industry is competing for. The law adds a demand signal for serving capacity, not a limit on it.

What the data does not show is how the law is enforced, what penalties attach, or whether other Washington bills covering AI failed or remain pending. One enacted law is a count, not a trend. It says Washington has acted once on a specific harm, and nothing more about the state's broader posture.

Washington has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Washington

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HB2225: Revised for 1st substitute: Regulating artificial intelligence companion chatbots. passed 2026-03-24

    The act regulates AI companion chatbots by requiring operators to disclose that the chatbot is artificial and not human, with recurring notifications. It imposes additional protections for minors, including restrictions on sexually explicit content and manipulative engagement techniques. It also requires operators to maintain protocols for detecting and responding to suicidal ideation or self-harm and to publicly disclose those protocols.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Washington. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
